summary: The exact encoder defect reproduces at the reporter's commit 40b3e15ddbd9a1067e181283d9900dd3f4d76ed7, but the prepared base already contains the correction associated with upstream commit 76603c6c2c9c276e0e9965d00fac97886fbe563a. Added focused regression and boundary coverage; no production source change was needed.

tests.command: execute encoding_dsv4.py from fetched issue commit 40b3e15ddbd9a1067e181283d9900dd3f4d76ed7 with dict and JSON-string tool arguments
tests.what_was_measured: The serving-path dict encoded as a nested DSML parameter named arguments, while the JSON string encoded filePath directly. Raw output is in reports/j-81083f6519f8/encoder_reproduction.txt.
3 tests passed with 2 subtests: serving normalization remains flat, JSON strings and dicts encode identically including nested/non-string values, and non-object arguments are rejected.
4 existing adjacent tests passed with 6 subtests, covering accepted object strings and rejected non-object arguments across the serving and DSV encoder boundaries.
No whitespace errors in the proposed changes.
The prepared interpreter does not include the ruff module, so this optional lint check could not run.

gpu_execution.evidence: The reported root cause and regression are deterministic CPU-only prompt encoding. No DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision weights or 4x H200 environment were available, and a gfx950 execution would not qualify that model configuration.

remaining_limitations: No full-model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision inference was run because the reported weights and 4x H200 configuration were unavailable.
The CPU encoder regression verifies the prompt-shape cause and correction, but cannot measure stochastic model output or semantic accuracy.
The prepared interpreter lacks ruff; pytest and git diff --check completed successfully.
